_readme: Predictions for scripts/notice-regression-probe.mjs. Write a real copy of this file BEFORE running the instrument -- it refuses to run without one (loadPredictions throws if the path is missing or if perTask is absent). Copy this file, fill in every task you are about to run, and pass the copy's path as the third argument. Field meanings -- perTask.<taskId>.discoveryCount: your predicted count of discovery-shaped run_command_readonly calls for that task (ls, find, fd, grep, rg, git grep, git ls-files -- the DISCOVERY regex in the recovered classify.mjs logic), an integer >= 0. perTask.<taskId>.falseNegativeResolves: only meaningful for T2 and T4, the two tasks item 90 records a false negative on (T2: 'the symbol does not appear anywhere in the repository', false -- it appears in ten places; T4: 'cannot locate an alternate path', false -- one whitelisted find locates it). Set true if you predict THIS run resolves that false negative, false if you predict it does not, null for every other task where the question does not apply. anyRefusal (top-level, not per-task): your prediction for whether ANY run_command_readonly call across every task you run is refused by checkCommandSafe -- true or false. Prior arms (item 90, item 91) recorded zero refusals across seventeen recovered commands, so false is the informative default; predicting true is itself a claim worth stating a reason for. rationale (top-level): free text stating the direction you expect and why -- required so a miss is checkable as a miss, not revised after the fact.
rationale: Example only -- T5 filled as a worked sample, matching arm C's own measured discovery count for T5 (item 90: arm C returns to arm A's exact counts). A real predictions file needs an entry for every task you are about to run (T1 through T7 for a full arm), with falseNegativeResolves set to true or false -- not left null -- for T2 and T4 specifically, since those are the only two tasks with a recorded false negative to predict against.
